title: Move one tenant without split ownership
objective: Synchronize one synthetic tenant, atomically fence its old owner and change its route, then measure requests and effects without touching other tenants.
preconditions: A browser with local JavaScript enabled; no service, subscription, login or package installation.
S005-fixture-v1 starts cedar, birch and maple on source with exclusive source fence 1.
The target copy starts at revision 0; each action consumes one explicit synthetic step.
actions: Replay source worker with captured fence 1
Inspect and reject an unrelated-route drift proposal

syntheticInput.clock: integer synthetic steps, initially 0; no wall clock, timer, random input or network

expectedAssertions: An unsynchronized or dual-owner migration blocks without effects.
A successful handoff increments the fence once and leaves exactly one target owner.
Configured routing is not an observed request; observation and per-site effects are separately recorded.
A captured source worker cannot write after the fence advances.
Other tenants' routes, data, ownership, observations and effects remain unchanged.
An unsafe unrelated-tenant proposal is identified and rejected rather than applied.
Unknown or extra input fails closed; native form Reset restores all state.

iac.reason: Only a portable local HTML/JS/CSS training bundle; no resources, registrations, deployments or management operations.

limits: Synthetic single-process atomicity and an integer fence are teaching models, not distributed ownership or database synchronization.
No native Azure, database, authentication, durability, concurrency, latency or availability proof.
No automatic rollback, live migration, persistent storage, external URL input or actual background worker.
Reset discards in-memory state; at most 80 steps and 80 trace entries per rehearsal.
Production runtime/auth design approval is not permission for resources, IaC, registration or spending.
B-S005 and the original source-demo acceptance gates remain separate.
